what_this_is: The MySQL application-SQL constructs Phase 4d recognises, in the same row shape as constructs.json. rule = a deterministic rewrite in appsql/rules_mysql.py; model = a faithful rewrite exists and needs judgement; manual = no correct automatic rewrite, a person decides. `marker` must appear in a conversion that claims the construct translated; `residue: true` means the MySQL form must be gone. Written against scripts/demo-app-mysql/ on 2026-09-29, whose statements run against the real DBMIG_MYSQL_APP tables.

constructs.name: backtick-quoted identifier
constructs.note: Backticks are a syntax error in PostgreSQL, and Phase 4c created every name lower-case and unquoted. A backticked RESERVED word is a different construct (RESERVED_WORD_OBJECT): 4c renamed that object, and only 4c knows to what.

constructs.name: IFNULL()
constructs.note: Identical two-argument semantics.

constructs.name: LIMIT offset, count
constructs.note: MySQL's two-argument LIMIT puts the OFFSET FIRST. Swapping the arguments by eye is the classic pagination bug: page 2 silently returns rows 11-20 of the wrong size.

constructs.name: CURDATE()
constructs.note: Same value: today's date in the session zone.

constructs.name: NOW()
constructs.note: MySQL NOW() is a zone-less DATETIME in the session zone, which is exactly LOCALTIMESTAMP. PostgreSQL's own now() is timestamptz -- legal, so the text may survive a model rewrite.

constructs.name: LOCK IN SHARE MODE
constructs.note: Same row-lock strength.

constructs.name: INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
constructs.postgres: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (<key>) DO UPDATE SET col = EXCLUDED.col
constructs.note: MySQL fires on ANY unique key; PostgreSQL only on the conflict target named. VALUES(col) becomes EXCLUDED.col, and the existing row's value is qualified by the table name.

constructs.name: INSERT IGNORE
constructs.note: Not the same: MySQL's IGNORE also turns data errors (truncation, a bad FK, a NOT NULL violation) into warnings and inserts something anyway. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING only skips duplicates -- the other errors now fail the statement, which is usually what the application should have had.

constructs.name: REPLACE INTO
constructs.note: REPLACE is DELETE then INSERT: it fires delete triggers, cascades ON DELETE foreign keys and assigns a NEW auto-increment id. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE keeps the row and its id. The rewrite is usually what was meant, and it changes behaviour -- say so.

constructs.name: GROUP_CONCAT()
constructs.note: SEPARATOR and ORDER BY move inside string_agg. MySQL truncates at group_concat_max_len (1024 bytes by default) without an error; string_agg does not, so the target can return longer values than the source ever did.

constructs.name: DATE_FORMAT()
constructs.note: The masks differ: %Y-%m-%d is YYYY-MM-DD, %H:%i:%s is HH24:MI:SS, %b is Mon, %M is FMMonth. A mask translated wrongly still runs.

constructs.name: STR_TO_DATE()
constructs.postgres: to_date() or to_timestamp(), by the target column's type
constructs.note: MySQL returns NULL for an unparseable string; PostgreSQL raises. And to_date drops the time, so a DATETIME target needs to_timestamp.

constructs.name: DATE_ADD / DATE_SUB / INTERVAL n UNIT
constructs.postgres: value +/- interval, or make_interval(...) for a bound amount
constructs.note: INTERVAL #{days} DAY cannot keep its bind inside a string literal: it becomes make_interval(days => #{days}) or #{days} * interval '1 day'. Adding a MONTH to 31 January clamps to month end on both engines.

constructs.name: IF(cond, a, b)
constructs.postgres: CASE WHEN cond THEN a ELSE b END
constructs.note: MySQL's IF() function has no PostgreSQL counterpart; the condition is a boolean, and a MySQL condition that relies on 0/1 truthiness needs an explicit comparison.

constructs.name: CONCAT()
constructs.note: MySQL CONCAT() returns NULL when any argument is NULL; PostgreSQL concat() skips NULLs and || propagates them. Whether the column is nullable decides which is faithful.

constructs.name: LIKE under a case-insensitive collation
constructs.postgres: ILIKE, or LIKE on citext -- as SCT 8795's decision says
constructs.note: Under MySQL's default utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, 'abc' LIKE 'A%' is true. PostgreSQL's LIKE is case-sensitive, so the same search returns fewer rows. The estate-wide collation decision (SCT 8795) decides ILIKE versus citext.

constructs.name: JSON_EXTRACT() / JSON_UNQUOTE()
constructs.postgres: jsonb operators: -> / ->> with a key path, or jsonb_path_query
constructs.note: MySQL paths are '$.a.b'; PostgreSQL uses 'a' ->> 'b' or a jsonpath. The column is jsonb on the target (Phase 4c). MySQL's own col->>'$.a' operator form is not detected here: string literals are blanked before scanning, and PostgreSQL spells the operator the same way, so a reviewer checks the path inside the quotes.

constructs.name: LAST_INSERT_ID() / selectKey
constructs.note: LAST_INSERT_ID() reads session state after the insert. RETURNING reads it in the same statement, which changes the mapper's structure rather than only its SQL.

constructs.name: SQL_CALC_FOUND_ROWS / FOUND_ROWS()
constructs.postgres: count(*) OVER () in the same query
constructs.note: The count lives in the session between TWO mapper statements. PostgreSQL has no such state, so the pair is redesigned into one query -- and FOUND_ROWS is deprecated in MySQL 8 anyway.

constructs.name: @user variable
constructs.postgres: a window function, or state kept by the application
constructs.note: Session variables assigned inside a SELECT (@rank := @rank + 1) depend on evaluation order MySQL itself does not guarantee. The intent -- usually a running number -- is a window function, which is a redesign of the query.

constructs.name: MATCH ... AGAINST (FULLTEXT)
constructs.postgres: to_tsvector(...) @@ websearch_to_tsquery(...) over a GIN index
constructs.note: Phase 4c did not emit the FULLTEXT index: the text-search configuration is a decision, and ranking differs between the engines.

constructs.name: ${} string interpolation
constructs.note: ${} must stay interpolated. Rewriting it to #{} turns a column name into a bound literal and breaks the query at runtime.

constructs.name: a reserved word as a table or column
constructs.postgres: the name Phase 4c chose (order -> order_tbl, group -> group_col)
constructs.note: Phase 4c renamed the object because its MySQL name is a PostgreSQL keyword. Only 4c knows the name it chose, so a statement naming it is reported for a person to apply 4c's mapping, never rewritten by guess.
